title: Monitoring ecological recovery of reclaimed wellsites: Protocols for quantifying recovery on forested lands
author: McIntosh, Drozdowski, et al.

steps.title: Compile potential site list
steps.instruction: Obtain a list of potential wellsites from the Alberta Energy Regulator (AER) and Alberta Environment and Parks (AEP) databases for the region(s) to be sampled in the given year.

steps.title: Rate candidate sites
steps.instruction: Determine Candidate Site Ratings using Appendix A, Table 5 and identify the highest‑rated candidate sites.

steps.title: Screen sites with additional data
steps.instruction: Review available data in AER, AEP and AbaData records to further screen the rated sites.

steps.title: Finalize candidate list
steps.instruction: Identify the final list of candidate sites and any lower‑priority sites in the vicinity that could be sampled if time permits.

steps.title: Obtain landowner permission
steps.instruction: Secure approval from the landowner or public‑land manager and notify the company responsible for the Forest Management Agreement; explain that work is government‑sponsored and cannot be refused.

steps.title: Conduct reconnaissance visit
steps.instruction: Visit each candidate site to confirm it is reclaimed, free of other disturbances, and accessible; reject permanently if not reclaimed or if access hazards (e.g., washed‑out or decommissioned roads) are present.

steps.title: Prepare access maps and route
steps.instruction: Create a predetermined access route to the site centre using GIS tools (Oil Trax or Avenza PDF); a modeler imports wellsite coordinates into the map; record GPS coordinates of the centre and the four corners on Datasheet #1 (Appendix B).

steps.title: Arrange ground‑disturbance notification
steps.instruction: Set up an Alberta OneCall account and submit a ground‑disturbance request at least 3 business days before sampling; contact pipeline owners for conflict information and verify line marking if no response is received.

steps.title: Compile site information package
steps.instruction: Assemble additional maps, site‑history descriptions, and hazard notes into a site information package; set compass declination for the location (record on Datasheet #1), note GPS accuracy, and, for complex access, record GPS locations of turnoffs, corners, landmarks, and parking spots with directions and distances.

steps.title: Prepare sampling supplies
steps.instruction: Before field work, label shipping tags using the convention “Region‑SiteNumber‑W/R‑Quadrant‑StartDepth” (e.g., DMG‑5‑W‑C‑30); place two 7‑lb polyethylene bags per sample and insert the pre‑labeled tag between them; gather stainless‑steel liners of known internal diameter and height, a double‑cylinder drop‑hammer core sampler (core diameter 2‑3 in / 5.1‑7.6 cm), two crescent wrenches, soil knife or metal spatula, Pam cooking spray, tape measure, two buckets with lids, hand pruners (optional, not used in pilot), Datasheet #5, analytical balance, drying oven capable of 105 °C, and a large waterproof bag to hold datasheets and sample bags.

steps.title: Collect soil cores
steps.instruction: Field procedure for each sampling point:

substeps.instruction: Select a smooth, relatively undisturbed surface at the designated sampling point.
Remove live vegetation with a quick kick of the boot.
Drive the double‑cylinder core sampler into the soil with drop‑hammer blows until the inner liner is filled; apply Pam spray if soil is dense to prevent compaction.
Rock the sampler in a circular motion to release the core, then carefully remove the undisturbed core.
Trim the core ends flush with the cylinder edge if necessary; if large coarse fragments or roots protrude, resample an adjacent spot and record the deviation on Datasheet #5.
Measure the start and end depths with a tape measure, record the core length on Datasheet #5.
Place the core in the pre‑labelled polyethylene bags, tie the bag closed, and store it in a larger durable plastic bag for transport.
Repeat the procedure in the same hole to collect the 15–30 cm depth sample.
Place each soil core sample in an oven set to 105 °C for 24 h.
After cooling, weigh the dry soil on an analytical balance and record the weight.

steps.title: Organize data and transport samples
steps.instruction: Keep paper bags available for any vegetation specimens; store all labelled polyethylene bags, datasheets, and the large waterproof bag together; verify that all labels and records are complete before transport.
